full_judgment: 8. Mr Pal next submits that the High Court Division held in contravention of law that since there was a salish between the parties Ext. 7 to the effect that defendant No. 2 would deliver khas possession in favour of the plaintiff there was no necessity of service under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. The notice is still necessary, he submits, as the alleged award was not binding between the parties not being made a rule of the Court and not being more than a mere scrap of paper having no legal effect. 	.
